entities.summary:
Robert Bakewell (1725–1795) was an English agricultural improver of Dishley, Leicestershire, famed for systematic selective breeding of livestock—especially sheep and cattle—during the British Agricultural Revolution. By inbreeding for heritable traits such as meat conformation and working with Disciple farmers, he helped shift animal husbandry from local mixed types toward more uniform, market-oriented breeds.

Bakewell’s methods, sometimes controversial among contemporaries, influenced New Leicester sheep and longhorn cattle improvement and inspired later breeders across Britain and beyond. His farm became a node of visiting improvers in an age of enclosure, fodder crops, and rising urban meat demand.

Economic and environmental historians treat him as a central agent of livestock modernisation that raised yields while reshaping rural landscapes and animal genetics.
